Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: $$(5x+3)^2=(\sqrt{3x+7})^2\Rightarrow25x^2+30x+9=3x+7\Rightarrow25x^2+27x+2=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{-27\pm\sqrt{27^2-4(25)(2)}}{50}=\frac{-27\pm23}{50}\Rightarrow x=-1\text{ or }x=-\tfrac{2}{25}.$$ Checking both in the original, only $$x=-\tfrac{2}{25}$$ satisfies the equation.

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.question_title: Solve the following equations using the quadratic formula.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.hint: Use the quadratic formula $$x=\dfrac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$$ for each equation and simplify the surds where possible.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: $$(a)\ a=1,b=3,c=1\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{-3\pm\sqrt{9-4}}{2}=\dfrac{-3\pm\sqrt5}{2}.$$ $$(b)\ a=1,b=-3,c=-2\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt{9+8}}{2}=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt{17}}{2}.$$ $$(c)\ a=1,b=6,c=6\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{-6\pm\sqrt{36-24}}{2}=\dfrac{-6\pm\sqrt{12}}{2}=-3\pm\sqrt3.$$ $$(d)\ a=1,b=-5,c=-2\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{5\pm\sqrt{25+8}}{2}=\dfrac{5\pm\sqrt{33}}{2}.$$ $$(e)\ a=3,b=10,c=-2\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{-10\pm\sqrt{100+24}}{6}=\dfrac{-10\pm\sqrt{124}}{6}=\dfrac{-10\pm2\sqrt{31}}{6}=\dfrac{-5\pm\sqrt{31}}{3}.$$ $$(f)\ a=4,b=-4,c=-1\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{4\pm\sqrt{16+16}}{8}=\dfrac{4\pm\sqrt{32}}{8}=\dfrac{4\pm4\sqrt2}{8}=\dfrac{1\pm\sqrt2}{2}.$$ $$(g)\ 4x^{2}-7x-2=0,\ a=4,b=-7,c=-2\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{7\pm\sqrt{49+32}}{8}=\dfrac{7\pm\sqrt{81}}{8}=\dfrac{7\pm9}{8}\Rightarrow x=2,\ -\tfrac14.$$ $$(h)\ a=11,b=2,c=-7\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{-2\pm\sqrt{4+308}}{22}=\dfrac{-2\pm\sqrt{312}}{22}=\dfrac{-2\pm2\sqrt{78}}{22}=\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt{78}}{11}.$$

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.question_text: Solve the following equations using the quadratic formula. Give your answers to three significant figures: (a) $$x^{2}+4x+2=0$$ (b) $$x^{2}-8x+1=0$$ (c) $$x^{2}+11x-9=0$$ (d) $$x^{2}-7x-17=0$$ (e) $$5x^{2}+9x-1=0$$ (f) $$2x^{2}-3x-18=0$$ (g) $$3x^{2}+8=16x$$ (h) $$2x^{2}+11x=5x^{2}-18$$.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.hint: Apply $$x=\dfrac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$$ to each, then evaluate the roots numerically and round to 3 s.f.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: $$(a)\ a=1,b=4,c=2\Rightarrow x=-2\pm\sqrt2\Rightarrow x\approx-0.586,-3.41.$$ $$(b)\ a=1,b=-8,c=1\Rightarrow x=4\pm\sqrt{15}\Rightarrow x\approx7.87,0.127.$$ $$(c)\ a=1,b=11,c=-9\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{-11\pm\sqrt{157}}{2}\Rightarrow x\approx0.765,-11.8.$$ $$(d)\ a=1,b=-7,c=-17\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{7\pm\sqrt{117}}{2}\Rightarrow x\approx8.91,-1.91.$$ $$(e)\ a=5,b=9,c=-1\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{-9\pm\sqrt{101}}{10}\Rightarrow x\approx0.105,-1.90.$$ $$(f)\ a=2,b=-3,c=-18\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt{153}}{4}\Rightarrow x\approx3.84,-2.34.$$ $$(g)\ 3x^{2}-16x+8=0,\ a=3,b=-16,c=8\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{16\pm\sqrt{160}}{6}\Rightarrow x\approx4.77,0.559.$$ $$(h)\ 3x^{2}-11x-18=0,\ a=3,b=-11,c=-18\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{11\pm\sqrt{337}}{6}\Rightarrow x\approx4.89,-1.23.$$

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: Multiply both sides by $$195x(x+2)$$ → $$195(x+2)+195x=\!28x(x+2).$$ Simplify → $$390x+390=\!28x^2+56x\Rightarrow28x^2-334x-390=0.$$ Divide by 2 → $$14x^2-167x-195=0.$$ Use the quadratic formula: $$x=\frac{167\pm\sqrt{167^2-4(14)(-195)}}{28}=\frac{167\pm\sqrt{34369}}{28}\approx\frac{167\pm185.3}{28}.$$ Hence $$x\approx12.6\text{ or }x\approx-0.65.$$ Since $x$ is positive, $$x\approx12.6.$$

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.question_text: Show that solving $$x^2 + 2bx + c = 0$$ by completing the square gives $$x = -b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - c}.$$
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: $$x^2 + 2bx = -c \Rightarrow (x + b)^2 - b^2 = -c \Rightarrow (x + b)^2 = b^2 - c \Rightarrow x + b = \pm \sqrt{b^2 - c} \Rightarrow x = -b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - c}.$$

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: Intercepts: $$y\text{-int }(0,10),\ x\text{-ints from }6x^2-19x+10=0\Rightarrow x=\tfrac{2}{3},\ \tfrac{5}{2}\Rightarrow\left(\tfrac{2}{3},0\right),\left(\tfrac{5}{2},0\right).$$ Vertex: $$x_v=\frac{19}{12},\ y_v=6\left(\tfrac{19}{12}\right)^2-19\left(\tfrac{19}{12}\right)+10=-\tfrac{121}{24}\Rightarrow\left(\tfrac{19}{12},-\tfrac{121}{24}\right).$$ Axis: $$x=\tfrac{19}{12}.$$

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.question_text: Sketch $$y=4-7x-2x^2$$: show intercepts, turning point, and line of symmetry.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: Intercepts: $$y\text{-int }(0,4),\ x\text{-ints from }-2x^2-7x+4=0\Rightarrow2x^2+7x-4=0\Rightarrow x=-4,\ \tfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow(-4,0),\left(\tfrac{1}{2},0\right).$$ Vertex: $$x_v=-\frac{-7}{2(-2)}=-\tfrac{7}{4},\ y_v=-2\left(-\tfrac{7}{4}\right)^2-7\left(-\tfrac{7}{4}\right)+4=\tfrac{81}{8}\Rightarrow\left(-\tfrac{7}{4},\tfrac{81}{8}\right).$$ Axis: $$x=-\tfrac{7}{4}.$$

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.question_text: Use the model to find fuel consumption at $$x=120$$ mph and comment on validity at very high speeds.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: $$y=-0.01(120)^2+0.975(120)+16=-144+117+16=-11\text{ mpg}.$$ A negative mpg is not physically meaningful ⇒ the quadratic model is unreliable at very high speeds; it is valid only over a moderate speed range.

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.question_text: (a) A fertiliser model $$g=6+0.03f-0.00006f^2$$ (tonnes/ha) gives yield for fertiliser $$f$$ (kg/ha). According to the model, how much grain per hectare with no fertiliser?
(b) One farmer currently uses $$f=20$$ kg/ha. How much **additional** fertiliser is needed to increase yield by 1 tonne/ha?
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.hint: Target $$g=6.576+1=7.576$$; solve for $$f$$ and choose the realistic root.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: Current $$g(20)=6+0.03(20)-0.00006(20)^2=6.576.$$ Solve $$6+0.03f-0.00006f^2=7.576\Rightarrow -0.00006f^2+0.03f-1.576=0$$ ⇒ $$f\approx59.65\text{ or }440.35.$$ The realistic choice near 20 is $$f\approx59.65,$$ so **additional** fertiliser $$\approx59.65-20=39.65\text{ kg/ha}$$ (≈$$39.6$$ kg/ha).

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.question_text: A football stadium has 25,000 seats. The football club knows from experience that they will sell 10,000 tickets if each ticket costs £30. (b) The total revenue (£$$r$$) can be calculated by multiplying the number of tickets sold by the price of each ticket. This gives $$r=p(M-1000p)$$. Rewrite this in the form $$A-B(p-C)^2,$$ where $$A,B,C$$ are constants to be found.
(c) Using the revenue equation or otherwise, determine how much the football club should charge per ticket to make the maximum amount of money.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.hint: Maximum occurs at the vertex when $$p=C$$.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: From $$r=400000-1000(p-20)^2,$$ the maximum occurs at $$p=20.$$ Therefore, the club should charge **£20 per ticket** for maximum revenue.

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.question_text: Lynn sold 80 cushions at £15 each. She expects to sell 10 more cushions for every £1 the price decreases. (a) The number sold is modelled by $$c=230-Hp$$ where £$$p$$ is the price and $$H$$ is a constant. Determine $$H$$.

Chapter 2 - Quadratics.question_text: Lynn’s revenue is $$r=p(230-Hp)$$. Using $$H=10$$, (b) rewrite in the form $$A-B(p-C)^2$$ and state $$A,B,C$$.
(c) Using the form in part (b) or otherwise, show Lynn can increase revenue by £122.50 by lowering the price, and state the optimum selling price.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.hint: Compare current revenue with the vertex value.
Chapter 2 - Quadratics.correct_answer: Current revenue at £15: $$r_0=15\times80=1200.$$ From $$r=1322.5-10(p-11.5)^2,$$ maximum revenue is $$A=1322.5$$ at $$p=C=11.5.$$ Increase: $$1322.5-1200=£122.5.$$ Therefore, lowering the price to **£11.50** maximises revenue and increases it by **£122.50**.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: $$\text{Use graph paper to draw accurately the graphs of }2y=2x+11\text{ and }y=2x^2-3x-5\text{ on the same axes}$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: $$\text{Rewrite each equation in the form }y=\dots\text{ and plot key points clearly}$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}2y&=2x+11\\y&=x+\frac{11}{2}\\[6pt]\text{This is a straight line with:}\\\text{slope }m&=1,\ \text{y-intercept }=\frac{11}{2}\\\text{Two points: }(0,\tfrac{11}{2}),\ (-\tfrac{11}{2},0)\\[8pt]y&=2x^2-3x-5\\\text{This is a parabola opening upwards}\\\text{Key points:}\\x&=0\Rightarrow y=-5\\x&=1\Rightarrow y=-6\\x&=2\Rightarrow y=-3\\\text{Plot these points and draw a smooth curve.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: $$\text{Use your graph to find the coordinates of the points of intersection}$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: $$\text{Points of intersection occur where the line and the curve cross}$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\text{From the graph, the line intersects the parabola at two points.}\\\text{Reading accurately from the graph:}\\\text{First intersection: }&(x,y)\approx(-2,\,3.5)\\\text{Second intersection: }&(x,y)\approx(1.5,\,7.0)\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: $$\text{Verify the intersection points by substitution into both equations}$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\textbf{Check }(-2,\,3.5):\\y&=x+\frac{11}{2}=-2+\frac{11}{2}=3.5\\y&=2(-2)^2-3(-2)-5=8+6-5=9\ \text{(not equal)}\\\text{Hence refine graph reading.}\\[6pt]\textbf{Exact solution (algebraic check):}\\x+\frac{11}{2}&=2x^2-3x-5\\2x^2-4x-\frac{21}{2}&=0\\4x^2-8x-21&=0\\x&=\frac{8\pm\sqrt{64+336}}{8}=\frac{8\pm20}{8}\\x&=3.5\ \text{or}\ -1.5\\[4pt]\textbf{Corresponding y-values:}\\x=3.5&:\ y=3.5+\frac{11}{2}=9\\x=-1.5&:\ y=-1.5+\frac{11}{2}=4\\[6pt]\therefore\ \text{Exact points of intersection are }&(3.5,\,9)\text{ and }(-1.5,\,4)\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Solve each inequality, then intersect the solutions.
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: From $$3x-6>x-4\Rightarrow2x>2\Rightarrow x>1$$ and $$4x+12>2x+17\Rightarrow2x>5\Rightarrow x>\tfrac{5}{2}$$; intersection: $$\{x\mid x>\tfrac{5}{2}\}=(\tfrac{5}{2},\infty).$$

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$2x-5<x-1$$ and $$7(x+1)>23-x$$.
Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$2x-3\ge2$$ and $$3(x+2)<12+x$$.
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: First $$2x\ge5\Rightarrow x\ge\tfrac{5}{2}$$; second $$3x+6<12+x\Rightarrow2x<6\Rightarrow x<3$$; intersection: $$\{x\mid \tfrac{5}{2}\le x<3\}=[\tfrac{5}{2},3).$$

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$15-x<2(11-x)$$ and $$5(3x-1)\ge12x+19$$.
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: First $$15-x<22-2x\Rightarrow x<7$$; second $$15x-5\ge12x+19\Rightarrow3x\ge24\Rightarrow x\ge8$$; intersection is $$\varnothing$$ (no real $$x$$).

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$3x+8\le20$$ and $$2(3x-7)\ge x+6$$.
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: First $$3x\le12\Rightarrow x\le4$$; second $$6x-14\ge x+6\Rightarrow5x\ge20\Rightarrow x\ge4$$; intersection: $$\{4\}.$$

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$5x+3<9$$ or $$5(2x+1)>27$$.
Use set notation to describe all $$x$$ such that $$4(3x+7)\le20$$ or $$2(3x-5)\ge\frac{7-6x}{2}$$.
Given $$A=\{x:3x+5>2\},\ B=\{x:\tfrac{x}{2}+1\le3\},\ C=\{x:11<2x-1\}$$ and $$A\cap(B\cup C)=\{x:p<x\le q\}\cup\{x:x>r\}$$, find $$p,q,r$$.
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Find each set, then compute $$B\cup C$$ and intersect with $$A$$.
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: $$A=(-1,\infty),\ B=(-\infty,4],\ C=(6,\infty)$$ so $$B\cup C=(-\infty,4]\cup(6,\infty).$$ Then $$A\cap(B\cup C)=(-1,4]\cup(6,\infty).$$ Hence $$p=-1,\ q=4,\ r=6.$$

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-7x+10<0$$ and $$3x+5\le17.$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-x-6>0$$ and $$10-2x<5.$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$4x^2-3x-1<0$$ and $$4(x+2)<15-(x+7).$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-x-1<0$$ and $$14\le3x-2.$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-x-12>0$$ and $$3x+17>2.$$
Use set notation to describe $$x$$ such that $$x^2-2x-3<0$$ and $$x^2-3x+2>0.$$
Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$\frac{2}{x}<1.$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Multiply by x² and consider sign of x.
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: For x>0: 2<x ⇒ x>2; for x<0: 2>x ⇒ x<0; hence \boxed{x<0\text{ or }x>2}.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$5>\frac{4}{x}.$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Multiply both sides by x (consider sign).
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: For x>0: 5x>4⇒x>\tfrac45; for x<0: 5x<4⇒x<\tfrac45 (always true for x<0). Hence \boxed{x<0\text{ or }x>\tfrac45}.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$\frac{1}{x}+3>2.$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: For x>0: 1>-x ⇒ always true; for x<0: multiply gives 1<-x ⇒ x<-1. Hence \boxed{x>0\text{ or }x<-1}.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$6+\frac{5}{x}\ge\frac{8}{x}.$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: For x>0: 6x≥3⇒x≥\tfrac12; for x<0: 6x≤3⇒x≤\tfrac12 (always true for x<0). Hence \boxed{x<0\text{ or }x\ge\tfrac12}.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$25>\frac{1}{x^2}.$$
Find the set of values of x (x≠0) for which $$\frac{6}{x^2}+\frac{7}{x}\le3.$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Multiply by x² and solve quadratic inequality.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the range of k for which $$x^2-kx+(k+3)=0$$ has no real roots.
Find the range of p for which $$px^2+px-2=0$$ has real roots.
Find the set of values of x for which $$x^2-5x-14>0.$$
Find the set of x for which $$2(3x-1)<4-3x.$$
Find the set of x for which $$2x^2-5x-3<0.$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Find roots and take between interval.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Find the set of x for which both $$2(3x-1)<4-3x$$ and $$2x^2-5x-3<0.$$
Find the set of values of x (x≠3) for which $$\frac{5}{x-3}<2.$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: $$5<2(x-3)\Rightarrow x>5.5$$ when x>3; and $$5>2(x-3)\Rightarrow x<0.5$$ when x<3; hence \boxed{x<\tfrac12\text{ or }x>\tfrac{11}{2}}.$$

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: For $$k x^2 - 2kx + 3 = 0$$, prove that it has no real roots when $$0\le k<3.$$
For the simultaneous equations $$2kx - y = 4$$ and $$4kx + 3y = -2,$$ where k is a constant, (a) Show that y = –2. (b) Find x in terms of k.
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Use elimination: multiply first equation by 3 and add to second.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: Solve the equations $$x + 2y = 3$$ and $$x^2 - 4y^2 = -33.$$
Given $$x-2y=1$$ and $$3xy-y^2=8,$$ (a) Show that $$5y^2+3y-8=0.$$ (b) Find all pairs (x,y).
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Use substitution $$x=2y+1$$ into the second equation.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: By eliminating y from $$x+y=2$$ and $$x^2+xy-y^2=-1,$$ (a) show that $$x^2-6x+3=0$$. (b) Hence solve for x and y, giving results in the form $$a\pm b\sqrt6.$$
(a) Given that $$3^x = 9^{y-1},$$ show that $$x = 2y - 2.$$ (b) Solve the simultaneous equations $$x = 2y - 2$$ and $$x^2 = y^2 + 7.$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Use properties of indices and substitution.
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.correct_answer: (a) $$9^{y-1}=(3^2)^{y-1}=3^{2y-2}\Rightarrow x=2y-2.$$ (b) Substitute into second: $$(2y-2)^2=y^2+7\Rightarrow3y^2-8y-3=0\Rightarrow y=3,-\tfrac13,$$ hence $$x=4,-\tfrac83.$$ \boxed{(x,y)=(4,3),(-\tfrac83,-\tfrac13)}.

Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.question_text: (b) Solve the simultaneous equations $$x+2y=3$$ and $$x^2-2y+4y^2=18.$$
Chapter 3 - Equations and inequal.hint: Substitute $$x=3-2y$$ and simplify to quadratic in y.
